results.content: Analysis: High Debt Combined with Low Growth Leaves UK Economy with Insufficient Buffer Capacity. Golden Ten Data reported on May 5 that Nigel Green, CEO and founder of the international financial consultancy deVere Group, stated in a report that the United Kingdom's high level of public debt and weak economic growth make it vulnerable to shocks. UK government debt is close to 100% of GDP. Green noted that against a backdrop of sluggish growth and elevated debt, rising political uncertainty poses challenges for the UK due to its limited room for maneuver. results.title: Palantir Stock Forecast | Q1 Earnings in Focus - Capital.com
results.content: # Palantir stock forecast: Q1 earnings in focus. Palantir is a US software company due to report Q1 2026 results on 4 May, with investors also tracking NHS contract scrutiny in the UK and Project Maven in the US. Sentiment ahead of the Q1 2026 earnings release on 4 May 2026 after market close, with consensus expecting revenue of approximately $1.54 billion, is shaping near-term positioning as investors weigh prior-quarter US commercial revenue growth of 137% year-on-year against broader valuation concerns (MarketBeat, 27 April 2026). At the same time, the UK government's public consideration of invoking a break clause in Palantir's £330 million NHS Federated Data Platform contract has added uncertainty around the company's international commercial pipeline (The Register, 20 April 2026), while the Pentagon's March 2026 formalisation of Project Maven as a long-term programme of record continues to underpin Palantir's US defence revenue outlook (Military.com, 25 March 2026). As of 29 April 2026, third-party Palantir stock forecasts for 2026–2030 reflect a range of views shaped by Palantir's AI platform demand, US government contract momentum, and multiple compression across high-growth software names ahead of the Q1 2026 earnings report.

results.title: Two-in-five profit warnings of UK-listed businesses linked to Middle East war - Consultancy.uk
results.content: Part of Consultancy.org Consultancy.uk. *Almost half of the profit warnings for FTSE-listed companies related in the first three months of 2026 related to policy change and geopolitical uncertainty, a new study suggests. The number of profit warnings from listed companies in the UK fell to its lowest in four years in 2025, with 240 firms issuing them. 2026 has seen this trend continue, with the first quarter seeing 55 profit warnings – a fall from the first three months of 2025, which saw 62. Jo Robinson, EY-Parthenon financial restructuring leader, commented, “The slower pace of profit warnings at the end of last year may have continued into early 2026, but UK-listed companies now face a prolonged period of uncertainty following the conflict in the Middle East. A record 49% of the 55 profit warnings issued by UK-listed companies in 2026’s first quarter cited the impact of policy change and geopolitical uncertainty as a leading factor. **EY-Parthenon** is not a United Kingdom partner of Consultancy.org. **EY-Parthenon** is a Local partner of Consultancy.org in Netherlands.
